claim: Spliceosomes consist of the U1, U2, and U4/U6.U5 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) and multiprotein Prp19-complex as major building blocks, plus many transiently interacting splicing factors.
source: Spliceosomes consist of the U1, U2, and U4/U6.U5 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) and multiprotein Prp19-complex as major building blocks, plus many transiently interacting splicing factors (Wahl et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wahl et al., 2009

claim: Spliceosomal machinery recognizes and assembles stepwise at splice sites with U1 at 5'SS and U2 at the 3'SS/branch site to form pre-spliceosomes.
source: This machinery recognizes and assembles stepwise at splice sites (SS) (U1 at 5'SS and U2 at the 3'SS/branch site) to form pre-spliceosomes, which are subsequently remodeled into catalytically active spliceosomes.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge in the field

claim: Pre-spliceosomes are subsequently remodeled into catalytically active spliceosomes.
source: This machinery recognizes and assembles stepwise at splice sites (SS) (U1 at 5'SS and U2 at the 3'SS/branch site) to form pre-spliceosomes, which are subsequently remodeled into catalytically active spliceosomes.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge in the field

claim: Pre-spliceosomes can form on multi-intron pre-mRNAs through at least two different pathways: cross-intron interactions and cross-exon interactions.
source: Pre-spliceosomes can form on multi-intron pre-mRNAs through at least two different pathways. An intron can be recognized a) via cross-intron interactions leading directly to a catalytically active spliceosome, or b) via cross-exon interactions where the exons flanking an intron are first defined, after which cross-intron interactions between adjacent cross-exon complexes lead to spliceosome assembly (Moldón and Query, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Moldón and Query, 2010

claim: On human pre-mRNAs, which characteristically harbor multiple long introns and short exons, exon definition predominates.
source: On human pre-mRNAs, which characteristically harbor multiple long introns and short exons, exon definition predominates (Berget, 1995; Fox-Walsh et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Berget, 1995 and Fox-Walsh et al., 2005

claim: Splicing is greatly enhanced when a 5'SS is present across the exon downstream of an intron.
source: Indeed, splicing is greatly enhanced when a 5'SS is present across the exon downstream of an intron, highlighting the importance of exon definition in humans (Talerico and Berget, 1990; Yue and Akusjärvi, 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Talerico and Berget, 1990 and Yue and Akusjärvi, 1999

claim: Cross-exon pre-spliceosomes can transition into cross-intron pre-spliceosomes, each having a distinct protein composition.
source: Cross-exon pre-spliceosomes can transition into cross-intron pre-spliceosomes, each having a distinct protein composition; the latter can then productively splice the pre-mRNA (Chiara and Reed, 1995; Schneider et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chiara and Reed, 1995 and Schneider et al., 2010

claim: Cross-intron pre-spliceosomes can productively splice the pre-mRNA.
source: Cross-exon pre-spliceosomes can transition into cross-intron pre-spliceosomes, each having a distinct protein composition; the latter can then productively splice the pre-mRNA (Chiara and Reed, 1995; Schneider et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chiara and Reed, 1995 and Schneider et al., 2010

claim: Single-molecule approaches have proven invaluable for elucidating the kinetic pathways and subcomplex dynamics involved in spliceosome assembly in S. cerevisiae.
source: In S. cerevisiae, where the cross-intron pathway predominates, single-molecule approaches have proven invaluable for elucidating the kinetic pathways and subcomplex dynamics involved in spliceosome assembly (Semlow et al., 2016; Warnasooriya and Rueda, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Semlow et al., 2016 and Warnasooriya and Rueda, 2014

claim: 20 ± 2% (s.d.) of PIP85A pre-mRNA was converted to spliced products after 40 mins in human cell line HEK293 nuclear extract.

claim: 1.1 ± 0.7% (s.e.) of surface-tethered pre-mRNA molecules lost intron fluorescence in the absence of ATP.
